events.title: The Day of Prayer for the Legal Protection of Unborn Children
events.shortBlurb: After the Roe v. Wade decision of this day, the Church in the United States set January 22 aside for prayer and penance for the unborn…
body: On 22 January 1973 the Supreme Court of the United States handed down its decision in Roe v. Wade, striking down the laws of the states that protected unborn children and establishing abortion on demand across the nation. The Catholic bishops answered with immediate and sustained opposition, reaffirming the Church's constant teaching that human life must be respected from conception.

The General Instruction of the Roman Missal appoints the anniversary, in all the dioceses of the United States, a Day of Prayer for the Legal Protection of Unborn Children: a day of penance for violations to the dignity of the human person committed through acts of abortion, and of prayer for the full restoration of the legal guarantee of the right to life.

The observance is kept with Masses, vigils, and acts of reparation, and a proper Mass formulary for the gift of human life may be celebrated. When 22 January falls on a Sunday, the day of prayer is observed on the following day.

sources.text: United States Conference of Catholic Bishops, Day of Prayer for the Legal Protection of Unborn Children (usccb.org)
